correctness.rationale: The complete recursive generation has unique root/component decomposition, yielding 16,752 and 17,568 states. The seven-tube ridge graph has 58,632 and 61,488 edges and degree seven throughout. Every ridge neighbor was independently verified by parent-child rotations. All 8! vertex permutations yield exactly 48 and 16 base automorphisms, enabling exhaustive orbit-weighted BFS from 355 and 1,098 orbit representatives. All source BFS distances span every state and reproduce the twenty-bin histogram and eccentricity profile; pair totals equal the exact binomial coefficients. A separate all-source C++ BFS produced the same 20-bin counts. No extrapolation from finite samples is used.

value.rationale: This resolves the complete shortest-rotation metric on two canonical eight-vertex connected cubic input graphs; state spaces exceed 16,000 and there are over 140 million unordered tree pairs in each. They have the same radius 17 and diameter 20 but substantially different antipodal-pair and eccentricity distributions, while each has exactly 16 symmetry orbits of diametral-eccentric states. This motivated structural comparison is not a routine restatement of the general diameter bounds and provides exact benchmarks for tree-rotation reconfiguration.
